note: precommitted from the committed case/subject tables and authored set-up; brackets tabulated with the reference loop listing below, refitted only against the CAPTURED loop listing

phases.teofc: the probe's PlayerLoop after-marker of PostLateUpdate.TriggerEndOfFrameCallbacks (not a coroutine)
phases.wfeof: an actual resume of the probe's WaitForEndOfFrame coroutine

end_of_frame.question: does the batchmode GPU Editor resume a WaitForEndOfFrame coroutine, and where relative to the teofc point

outcomes.NOT_DELIVERED: no resume of the coroutine through the final step (wfeof cases NOT_ISSUED)
outcomes.IN_TEOFC_LEAF: every resume between the two markers of PostLateUpdate.TriggerEndOfFrameCallbacks, i.e. before the teofc point of the same step
outcomes.AFTER_TEOFC_POINT: every resume after the teofc point of its step and before the next leaf (same position string as the teofc point; separated by the raw point order)
outcomes.OTHER_POSITION: every resume at one or more other bracket positions (listed)
outcomes.MIXED: resumes of more than one of the classes above

end_of_frame.precommitted: unknown; every outcome is admissible and none gates a capture

priors.quote: in batch mode the Game view does not render, so the screen camera, OnGUI and WaitForEndOfFrame never run

limits: teofc is a PlayerLoop marker position after PostLateUpdate.TriggerEndOfFrameCallbacks, never a WaitForEndOfFrame coroutine; its cases measure a Destroy requested at that loop position only.

Whether a batchmode GPU Editor resumes WaitForEndOfFrame coroutines at all is a precommitted unknown (END_OF_FRAME_OUTCOMES). If NOT_DELIVERED, the coroutine-phase Destroy (go.wfeof) is NOT_ISSUED and both it and per-subject WaitForEndOfFrame delivery after a Destroy stay unmeasured by this fixture; no windowed or other fallback capture is implied.
Brackets name the marker pair a callback ran between, never a private Unity node; a last-label position is not a node claim.

Reentrancy: one isolated, deterministic case only (subject reenter, its own step 19 and frames): a second Destroy of the same GameObject from its own OnDisable. Descriptive, never fitted or intersected; reentrancy from other callbacks, objects or phases is unmeasured.
Positive delays (Destroy(obj, t > 0)) and DestroyImmediate are unmeasured; no timing policy is fitted.
The relative order of per-frame callbacks (Update, LateUpdate, wfeof) between subjects is not recorded (counts only).
